concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A finite-control machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes, each head moving at most one cell per step.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes.

concepts.gloss: The tensor product of vector spaces or linear maps, whose dimension is the product of the factors' dimensions; tensor powers act factorwise on multi-index arrays.

evidence.quote: The ambient label space is $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$ with its tensor bilinear form.

concepts.name: Nondegenerate bilinear forms and orthogonal complements
concepts.gloss: A symmetric bilinear form pairs vectors; a subspace is nondegenerate when the form restricted to it has no kernel, and then the space splits as the subspace plus its orthogonal complement.

concepts.gloss: The established deterministic O(n log n) multitape integer multiplier, used here only as an ordinary subroutine on short records.

Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine

concepts.name: Lexicographic array layout and logical volume
concepts.gloss: Arrays on a product of address fields are stored on tape in lexicographic order with addresses implicit, and their cost is measured against the logical volume V, the number of stored data bits.

evidence.quote: is stored in lexicographic order, with the first coordinate most significant.
The \emph{logical volume} $V$ is the number of stored data bits.

concepts.name: Elementary stream operations
concepts.gloss: Linear-time tape primitives: permuting or moving single digits, splitting on a digit and merging, and splitting rows cyclically into a fixed number of streams.

evidence.quote: Each of the following operations on an array of volume $V$ takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes

concepts.name: Controlled shifts
concepts.gloss: Linear-time updates that add to a target address field an offset computed from earlier control fields (or multiply it by a fixed unit), implemented by splitting and remerging each fiber.

evidence.quote: Controlled shifts and fixed rational scalings
The next operations are linear because their target field follows their control fields.

concepts.name: Scratch restoration
concepts.gloss: The transparent-computation trick of subtracting a scratch register's effect, computing, adding, and uncomputing, so that the net result is independent of arbitrary initial scratch values.

evidence.quote: This cancellation of arbitrary initial scratch values is a linear instance of the restoration construction for transparent computation

concepts.name: Three-element-subset intersection construction
concepts.gloss: The Frankl–Wilson-style use of 3-subsets of a 100-element set, where gather and scatter produce coefficients depending on intersection size and side wires cancel the unwanted ones, giving y ← y + x.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted coefficients.

concepts.name: Bank-exchange linear network
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network of pointwise gates on wires (roles) that, in three stages, exchanges two banks of values with prescribed signs while restoring every auxiliary scratch wire.

evidence.quote: We construct two fixed linear networks that exchange two banks of values while restoring every auxiliary value.
A wire's fixed place in the network is called its role.

concepts.name: Row splitting into role streams
concepts.gloss: Rows of an array are distributed cyclically among the network's W roles so each role stream has volume V/W, and recursive calls are scheduled depth-first on a fixed set of tapes by parking inactive streams on a stack.

evidence.quote: Distribute rows cyclically among the $W$ roles, padding the row count
A fixed-tape depth-first schedule.

concepts.name: Frames and the common-frame identity
concepts.gloss: Each network vertex gets an invertible linear operator (frame) giving the stored array's representation; since a common frame commutes with pointwise gates, the network implements the endpoint frame ratio on every role.

evidence.quote: We call $D_v$ its frame: the stored
Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate

concepts.name: Subspace labels and orthogonal residuals
concepts.gloss: Nested nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed m-dimensional tensor space are attached to the network's vertices, and the dimension of each edge's orthogonal residual counts the smaller operations that edge needs.

evidence.quote: the \emph{orthogonal residual} is the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside
The saving will come from keeping the total dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to $N$.

concepts.name: Rank deficit and recursive power saving
concepts.gloss: The total number s of smaller calls satisfies s < Wm, so a recursion with parameter growth m and volume split W gives a cost factor e^τ with τ < 1 instead of e.

evidence.quote: The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.
This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Lower triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: Every rational matrix of rank a factors as E₁ΠE₂ with invertible lower triangular E₁, E₂ and a partial permutation Π with a ones (a reversed Bruhat factorization).

evidence.quote: The required factorization is the Bruhat factorization for arbitrary matrices, with coordinate order reversed

concepts.name: Rational address shear
concepts.gloss: The address permutation (H,D) ↦ (H+AD, D) on two groups of fields, performed with exactly rank(A) smaller field interchanges plus linear work.

evidence.quote: The cost of a rational matrix shear
For a matrix $M$, the frame $\Phi_M$ moves the array entry

concepts.name: Fast address-chunk interchange
concepts.gloss: A tape procedure that interchanges two disjoint u-bit address fields of an array in O(V u^τ) time for a fixed τ < 1, by running the bit network with shear frames and recursing on smaller interchanges.

evidence.quote: Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.
Arbitrary-width interchange

concepts.gloss: The length-q transform averaging inputs times powers of e^{∓2πi/q}, normalized by 1/q so it is a contraction.

evidence.quote: Each normalized Fourier transform above is a contraction

concepts.name: Multidimensional Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The tensor product of one-dimensional transforms over several axes, applied to arrays indexed by a product of cyclic groups.

evidence.quote: it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for this convolution by multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two.

concepts.name: Radix-digit reduction to convolution
concepts.gloss: Splitting each n-bit input into b-bit digits turns integer multiplication into convolution of short nonnegative integer coefficient lists, followed by carry propagation.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Error accounting through contractions
concepts.gloss: Since every exact map used is a contraction, errors of approximate subroutines add when composed, which bounds the final numerical error.

evidence.quote: Composing such algorithms adds their errors

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey and van der Hoeven's identity expressing a Fourier transform of prime length s through one of nearby power-of-two length t, via Gaussian-weighted contractions.

evidence.quote: Gaussian resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a power-of-two tensor transform.

concepts.name: Resampling with retained permutations
concepts.gloss: A variant of Gaussian resampling that keeps the source and target coordinate permutations inside the transform identity instead of executing them as sorts.

evidence.quote: We retain both permutations in the transform formula and compute that formula directly.
Resampling without executing the two permutations

concepts.name: Prime source lengths
concepts.gloss: Distinct odd primes s_i chosen just below the power-of-two axis lengths t_i, so their product fills a fixed fraction of the padded box while leaving the separation resampling needs.

evidence.quote: The distinct prime lengths $s_i$ must be close to the powers of two

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: An algebra isomorphism from one cyclic convolution of length S = ∏ s_i to a multidimensional cyclic convolution on pairwise coprime axes, implemented by triangular controlled shifts and axis moves.

evidence.quote: placed on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution
Agarwal and Cooley used the Chinese remainder theorem

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Multiplying by quadratic phases (chirps) before and after a cyclic convolution computes a Fourier transform, here including its target permutation.

evidence.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform,

concepts.name: Source-permutation cancellation
concepts.gloss: The source permutation retained in both forward transforms cancels against the opposite-sign transform when computing a convolution.

evidence.quote: the source permutation retained during resampling cancels across the two forward source transforms

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.gloss: Complex polynomials reduced modulo y^r + 1 with r a power of two, where multiplication by a power of y is a signed cyclic shift of coefficients.

evidence.quote: is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two.

concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The formal polynomial variable, whose powers act as roots of unity in the ring.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in one ring element, a power of two.

concepts.name: Coefficient phase twist
concepts.gloss: Multiplying coefficient k by e^{πik/r} turns cyclic convolution in the last axis into negacyclic multiplication modulo y^r + 1.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Normalized butterfly
concepts.gloss: The two-point map H₀(u,v) = ((u+v)/2, (u−v)/2), the basic step of radix-two decimation-in-frequency transforms.

evidence.quote: the decimation-in-frequency step pairs $z_k$ with $z_{k+t/2}$

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: Nussbaumer's Fourier transform over the polynomial ring, where powers of y serve as roots of unity so twiddles are signed shifts and the transform is butterflies plus monomial multiplications.

evidence.quote: synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle
Powers of $y$ then serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes

concepts.name: Binary phase frames
concepts.gloss: Frames for the complex network built from the kernel C = H·diag(1,i)·H and quadratic-form phases over F₂, so each edge change is one two-point kernel per orthonormal residual basis vector.

evidence.quote: Its phase-frame difference
The binary phase interface

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: XORing corresponding selected bits of two address chunks using eight cyclic shifts of whole chunks with guard values, then deterministically repairing the small set of exceptional addresses by sorting.

evidence.quote: Packed selected-bit addition on one rectangle
then corrects an explicitly bounded set of addresses

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: Applying the butterfly H₀ on one selected bit in each of up to d address chunks at once in O(V d^λ′) time, λ′ < 1, by running the complex network with phase frames recursively and truncating once at the end.

evidence.quote: Simultaneous normalized butterfly layer

concepts.name: Synthetic transform layout and cost
concepts.gloss: The tape layout that places the selected bits of all axes at common offsets in consecutive chunks, so each synthetic transform round is one simultaneous layer, with frequencies left in a retained bit-reversed order.

concepts.name: Signed Kronecker packing
concepts.gloss: Multiplying polynomials with signed coefficients by evaluating them at a large power of two, multiplying the resulting integers, and extracting centered coefficients.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution
Signed packing and normalized ring multiplication

concepts.name: Normalized convolution over the polynomial ring
concepts.gloss: Computing normalized cyclic convolution of arrays of ring elements by two forward synthetic transforms, pointwise packed products in the retained order, and the opposite transform.

evidence.quote: Convolution from the retained transform layout
Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record permutation $LB$ to both operands.

concepts.name: Exact recovery by rounding and carries
concepts.gloss: Once the approximate coefficient error is below 1/2, rounding gives the exact integer coefficients, and radix carry propagation gives the binary product.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$, and propagates carries to obtain the exact binary product.

concepts.name: Parameter choice and cost table
concepts.gloss: Fixed rational exponents (τ, λ′, ε, c, δ, …) and size parameters chosen so every row of the normalized cost table is at most p^{1−2κ}.

evidence.quote: A compatible choice of rational parameters makes all terms in its cost table fit Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
These constants are deliberately conservative; no optimization is claimed.

evidence.quote: We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers
for every input length and disproves the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture
